title: Asymptotic complexity of GAD and GADec on Goldreich PRGs
summary: Derive tight asymptotic complexities for the source GAD and GADec attacks on its XOR-AND and XOR-MAJ predicate families.

formal_statement.body: For every XOR-AND and XOR-MAJ predicate family considered by the source, derive and rigorously justify the asymptotic attack complexity of both the source guess-and-determine (GAD) and guess-and-decode (GADec) attacks. State the seed-length, stretch, locality, sample, guessing, and success regime needed to interpret each asymptotic bound.

scope.domain: Cryptanalysis of Goldreich local pseudorandom generators
assumptions: The PRG and random-neighborhood model are those of the source
The attacked predicates are the source XOR-AND and XOR-MAJ families
The algorithms under analysis are the source GAD and GADec attacks
scope.unresolved_remainder: No rigorous asymptotic complexity analysis was found for the source GAD and GADec attacks across the considered XOR-AND and XOR-MAJ predicate families; later work analyzes a different attack and therefore does not settle this task.

progress.summary: The source leaves rigorous asymptotic analysis of its GAD and GADec attacks on the broader XOR-AND and XOR-MAJ families for future work.
